lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: populations and samples

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read the example first. You are not expected to know this yet.

items.prompt: A researcher wants to know about all 400 students at Lincoln Middle School. She randomly selects 40 of them to survey. What is the sample in this situation?

steps: The population is every member of the group being studied: all 400 students.
The sample is the subset actually surveyed: the 40 randomly selected students.
workedSolution.answer: The 40 randomly selected students at Lincoln Middle School

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Try each one. If you get stuck, write what you do know and move on.

items.prompt: A student uses a random number generator to select 6 shoppers at a grocery store from the full list, then surveys them. Is this sampling method likely to produce a representative sample?
choices: Yes, likely representative — every member had a fair, known chance of being chosen.
No, likely not representative, because the population is too large.
No, likely not representative — the method favors certain members over others.
Yes, likely representative, because the sample size is large enough.

items.prompt: In a random sample of 7 commuters on a train line, 3 preferred a proposed schedule change. Based on this sample, about how many of the 35 commuters on a train line would you expect to prefer a proposed schedule change?
Five random samples of the same population produced these mean scores: 17, 20, 14, 20, 14. What is the range of these sample estimates?

A population has 1471 commuters on a train line. Student A takes a random sample of 8. Student B takes a random sample of 54. Both use proper random selection. Whose sample is more likely to give an estimate closer to the true population value?
choices: Both are equally likely to be accurate, because both are random.
Student A's sample of 8, because smaller samples are easier to analyze.
Neither sample is reliable unless it includes the entire population.
Student B's sample of 54, because larger random samples tend to produce more consistent, accurate estimates.

items.prompt: A student surveys 54 visitors to a science museum using a simple random sample and records the results. Is it valid to generalize this result to all 2106 visitors to a science museum?
choices: Yes, because the sample size is large enough regardless of how it was chosen.
Yes, because the sample was selected randomly, so it is likely representative of the population.
No, because samples can never be generalized to a population.
No, because the sample was not randomly selected, so it may not represent the population.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Show what you can do so far. This sets the starting point, not a grade.

items.prompt: A sample of 5 values is: 11, 13, 13, 15, 13. What is the median of this data set?
A data set has 5 values: 14, 15, 15, 15, 11. What is the new mean if an outlier of 59 is added to the data set, making 6 values in all?
